### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **25** documentable anchor(s).

**38** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fe1249b70292e4e8ba3188ddbbf96383d5400087`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **43** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fe1249b70292e4e8ba3188ddbbf96383d5400087` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `644838bcb314ec924fc5801e7444e34bf271daf4` — the merge of head `921ec56ae65b22a353d15d9ef76ab102b9090274` into base `fe1249b70292e4e8ba3188ddbbf96383d5400087`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 644838bcb314ec924fc5801e7444e34bf271daf4 && git checkout 644838bcb314ec924fc5801e7444e34bf271daf4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fe1249b70292e4e8ba3188ddbbf96383d5400087 921ec56ae65b22a353d15d9ef76ab102b9090274 && git checkout -B drift-repro fe1249b70292e4e8ba3188ddbbf96383d5400087 && git merge --no-ff 921ec56ae65b22a353d15d9ef76ab102b9090274

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fe1249b70292e4e8ba3188ddbbf96383d5400087
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fe1249b70292e4e8ba3188ddbbf96383d5400087` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review of #32101 (#31697, action) at head 921ec56a: PASS on everything except Deviation 1, which needs one change.**

- **Ruling 6729825528 letter A is carried out.** Two holders on the same object, with no package named, answer 409 naming both on every bare door: the engine's `executeAction`, bare REST, MCP `run_action`, and the object-less `/meta/action/NAME`. Qualified addresses reach each holder. `Narrowing: yes` and `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` are declared, with a first-party count of 0.
- **The G2 obligation is met, and the classification is by source.** An owner-less row is the environment's only when `sys_metadata` holds that row. Otherwise it is the platform's, and `_provenance` is never read. Host code and a plugin beside a package are refused, naming both.
- **The B shape holds.** Co-owners, a package with no namespace, base/system/sys, built-ins and API stay refused. The stored-references report shows `sealedClashes: []` on showcase and crm.

**Deviation 1 must change (red line 2).** `bareRouteHolderRefusal` catches every throw and falls through to the rungs. When there are two packages on the same object, those rungs answered "the object's own". So in a production deployment whose store read fails, the REST layer can resolve a declaration by rung while the refusal is skipped. The engine's two-owner refusal covers code handlers only, not every target an action declaration can carry. The fix that keeps the fixtures:
- **Capability absent → fall through.** When no `protocol` / `metadata` service resolves, or the merged listing is not a function (the 30 fixtures with no metadata store), nothing can hold two items, so the pre-check judges nothing.
- **Capability present but the read throws → fail closed** through the existing `degraded` answer (503), never the rungs.
- **Pin:** a protocol whose listing throws answers `degraded`, and ablating the pin turns it red.

Re-read only the delta once it is pushed. Contract review is the seat's.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `921ec56ae65b22a353d15d9ef76ab102b9090274`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-actions.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/objectql/src/bound-action-collision-report.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin-authored-actions.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-bare-name-one-holder-ai-family.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-bare-name-one-holder-request-family.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions-addressed-route.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/bare-name-one-holder-request-family.dogfood.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/stored-references.integration.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/action-package-addressing.ts, packages/objectql/src/action-handler-coordinate.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (the authored-action resync and its store read), packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useNavActionDispatch.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/consoleServerAction.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/marketplaceApi.ts, examples/app-todo/src/actions/register-handlers.ts (read in the PR tree, not reviewed). Not reviewed: .changeset/31697-action-names-per-namespace.md (prose face; read for ②).

Inputs: card #31697 (body and all 8 comments), PR #32101 (body, 15 files, net diff against the merge base 48f18b58 on main), the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built or run.

Check-runs on the head when this record was written: 25 completed with success (Build Core, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint and Repo Gates and its eight Lint rows, Live E2E UI, Test UI, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, three of four Type Check rows, Plan Test Core shards, filter, Auto Label, Flag docs). Still in progress: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8 and Type Check · workspace. No row failed. The verdict below does not depend on the nine open rows; a PASS would have had to wait for them.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Install side, object-less action joins `NAMESPACE_SCOPED_BARE_NAME_TYPES`: two packages of two namespaces may each hold one object-less action name. Right. It is one entry in the shared switch, judged by the shared predicate `bareNameHoldersMeet`; a co-owner, a package with no namespace, base/system/sys, a built-in name, and the API and function types stay refused, each with a pin in the request-family test.
2. Engine, `executeAction` with no `packageId` while two code owners hold a handler under one key: refused 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, naming every owner. Right for two packages (ruling 6729825528, letter A). For a package beside host code or a plugin, see ③ flag 4.
3. MCP bare `run_action`, object-bound pair: goes through `pickActionHolder` where it answered the first listed. Right. One undeclared side effect, finding F2.
4. REST bare `/actions/:object/:action`: a pre-check over the merged listings refuses two holders. Right when the listing answers. Wrong when it throws, finding F1.
5. `/meta/action/NAME` with no package, two packages' object-less action: refused 409 before any layer is read; `?package=` reaches each. Right, and it matches seat ruling Q1 A (object-bound reads are left to `getItem`). Two gaps, findings F3 and F4.
6. Owner-less declarations classified by source: the environment's only when the store holds a package-less row; anything else is the platform's. Right in direction, and `_provenance` is not read. The key it matches on is too loose, finding F5.
7. `BUILT_IN_BARE_NAMES.action` stays empty. Right: I found no fixed-name object-less action request under `packages/**/src` or `ui/**/src`. The two fixed-name requests the UI and cloud-connection make (`sys_package/install_package`) are object-bound, outside this set, see F7.
8. No public export is removed or renamed. Added: `environmentStoredActionNames`, `EnvironmentStoredActionNames` (runtime), `SchemaRegistry#refuseAmbiguousObjectLessAction` (objectql), an optional eighth parameter on `resolveActionByName`. Additive.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

The changeset moves `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` at `minor`, with `Metadata-protocol: added`. That matches the rule in AGENTS.md: the kind is `added` (a second namespace may now declare the name), `added` takes at least `minor`, and the narrowing keeps its BREAKING banner and its ADR-0087 marker (`not-required`, no-migration-prescription; the fix is the qualified address the refusal names). The three packages are the three whose `src` the diff moves; `cli` and `qa/dogfood` change tests only. `Check Changeset` is green. The PR body and the changeset carry the same two declaration lines.

One sentence in the changeset is not true of the diff: "then it answers first, as before (ADR-0150 D3)". For an object-bound pair, MCP answered the first listed on base, not the environment's (F2). Prose face; fix it with F2.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. `open_questions`: empty in the dev report. Nothing to answer.
2. Deviation 1 (a listing that throws judges nothing): not accepted. Finding F1, must-fix.
3. Deviation 2 (dogfood co-owner refused by the override write gate, 403 `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`, before the one-holder door): accepted. The door's own co-owner refusal is pinned in-process in the request-family test.
4. Deviation 3 (claim lines): answered by the claim amendment 6762064600 on the card.
5. Escalated to the epic seat: the card body says a narrowing beyond the declared one goes to the maintainer before landing. The card thread shows the maintainer's letter for two packages on one object (6729825528) and the epic seat's obligation for a host row beside a package on an object-less name at `run_action` (6742974046). The diff goes further: the engine refuses a bare call when host code or a plugin holds a handler beside a package's on ANY key, object-bound included, and the flipped pin in `plugin-authored-actions.test.ts` (#30542) shows a call that ran on base and is now refused. The claim amendment says "the epic seat agreed", but that agreement is not on the card thread I was given. The epic seat should either confirm in writing that 6742974046 covers handler pairs on object-bound keys, or take it to the maintainer. First-party count is 0 by the PR's census.
6. The epic carry-in 6760055671 asks for a red-line review by the epic seat before landing. This record is not that review.
7. Security: nothing found that needs the owner seat. No security note was written.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing itself is sound: it makes the spec's own refusal (ADR-0150 D5, "ambiguous bare name answers 409 naming the candidates") real at the four bare doors, and the addressed doors reach each holder. It does not take a declared capability away at the consumer. The findings are about where the refusal leaks.

**F1 — must-fix. The bare REST door picks one of two holders when the listing read throws.** `bareRouteHolderRefusal` wraps the protocol resolve, both `readMergedItems` calls and `collectActionDeclarations` in a `try` whose `catch` returns `undefined`, and `resolveRouteActionDeclaration` then runs the old rungs. Rung 1 returns the routed object's embedded action from the in-memory schema without reading anything else. So for the exact case ruling A covers (one package embeds `convert` on `lead`, another binds a standalone `convert` to `lead`), a merged-listing read that throws serves the object's own declaration, as on base. For two standalone bound rows, the by-name rung serves the first registered. The engine backstop does not close this: it counts handler owners, and the resync's own docblock says flow, url and target-bound actions register no handler, so a pair where at most one side has an engine handler dispatches the picked declaration.

This is fail-open on a refusal the card's first two red lines make absolute ("no silent pick", "ambiguity is reported, never guessed"). It also contradicts three standing statements in the same file: `readMergedItems` ("a throw travels to the caller, never a fallback to the un-merged read"), the by-name rung ("never a cue to fall back to a copy that would run that item during the outage"), and the sibling addressed door, which answers `degraded` on the same read. The PR body's sentence "nothing is served from the failed read" is true and beside the point: the pick is served from the rungs.

It must fail closed. In production `resolveService` swallows its own resolution failures (the rung's comment says so), so what reaches this `catch` is a real read failure, not a missing service. Structural absence (no protocol, no metadata service, no list verb) already yields an empty declaration set without throwing and may keep judging nothing. A thrown read should answer `degraded`, as the store read ten lines below does. The 30 fixture failures the deviation cites are then a fixture question (a double that throws where the real service answers absent), not a reason to pick. Add a pin: listing throws, two holders on one object, the bare call is not served.

**F2 — should-fix. The bare REST door judges by the holder rule and then serves by rung precedence.** On a resolved answer `bareRouteHolderRefusal` discards what `pickActionHolder` returned. For an object-bound pair of a package's embedded action and an environment-stored standalone row of the same object and name, MCP now runs the environment's (D3: the environment answers first) while REST still returns the embedded one from rung 1. On base both doors answered the embedded one. So the diff changes MCP's answer for that pair without declaring it, and leaves the two bare doors disagreeing about one name, which is the mismatch carry-in 3 exists to remove. The CONTROL pin covers only the object-less shape, where the rungs happen to agree. Either serve the resolved holder's declaration from the pre-check, or pin and declare the object-bound case.

**F3 — should-fix. `/meta/action/NAME` does not apply the platform classification the other doors apply.** `refuseAmbiguousObjectLessAction` resolves over the registry, where an item registered with no package reads as the environment's own and answers first (the PR's own CONTROL pins this with `registerItem` and no package, which is a host registration, not a store row). REST and MCP classify the same row as the platform's and refuse it beside a package. So for a host row beside one package, the by-name read serves the host's definition while the action doors answer 409. Nothing runs, so this is not a pick of a handler, but it is a guess at the read door the PR brought under the rule, and it breaks the PR's own sentence that the platform "never answers first".

**F4 — should-fix. With one of two holders disabled, the bare REST call answers "degraded".** The merged listings withhold a disabled package, so the pre-check sees one holder and falls to the rungs. The by-name rung then calls the protocol read, whose new refusal counts registry holders, and the registry keeps a disabled package's item (the rung's comment says so). The thrown 409 lands in the rung's `catch` and is returned as `degraded`. Disabling one package is the operator's obvious remedy for a collision; after it, REST reports a metadata outage while MCP runs the enabled package's action. I read this off the code and did not run it; if the registry does drop a disabled package's holder, say where and this finding closes. The same `catch` mislabels the refusal in the F1 path for an object-less pair.

**F5 — should-fix. The source classifier matches on a looser key than the row's identity.** `packagelessOriginOf` calls a standalone row the environment's when the store holds ANY package-less action row of that name, whatever object it is bound to, and an embedded row the environment's when the store holds ANY package-less object row of that name, whether or not that row embeds the action. The action key everywhere else in this epic is (package, object, name). No request byte moves a row: `_provenance` and the definition are not read, and the store's `package_id` column decides. But an environment row `convert` on `account` makes a host row `convert` on `lead` read as the environment's, and it then answers first beside a package instead of being refused. Whether both rows survive the merged listing I could not settle by reading. Match the standalone row on its owner key as well as its name. Also, the PR says this is "the read the resync makes"; the resync skips `legacyOrganizationRowIds()` rows and this read does not (nit, same fix).

**F6 — should-fix, may close with a named card. First-party UI names no package on any action door.** `useNavActionDispatch` reads `getItem('action', name)` bare and `consoleServerAction.ts` builds the bare `/actions/OBJECT/ACTION` URL; neither file mentions a namespace or a package. So "first-party 0" holds for the narrowing only because no first-party composition has a colliding pair. Once a deployment uses the widening (two namespaces each ship object-less `digest`), neither package's nav item nor button works in the Console: both answer 409. That is fail-closed and loud, and no red line is crossed. But the epic carry-in asks for "readers before narrowing: every reader of the type resolves by (package, name)", and the Console reader does not. The widened capability is declared and not delivered at the first-party consumer, which is an implementation gap to be implemented, not left. Name the card that makes the Console address an action by its app's package (or file it) in the PR body before landing.

**F7 — nit, follow-up. Fixed-name object-bound requests are bare.** The Console and cloud-connection post to `/actions/sys_package/install_package` with no package. Under ruling A, any installed package that binds an action of that name to `sys_package` turns the marketplace install button into a 409. That is the ruling's letter and needs an admin install, so nothing changes here; it belongs with F6's card.

What held when I tried to break it: every bare door refuses and names every holder when the listing answers (pins on REST, MCP, engine and `/meta`); the qualified doors reach each holder (pins, and the dogfood addressed calls); a missing store reader (`find` absent, or the engine unavailable) classifies every package-less row as the platform's, which refuses rather than picks; a store read that throws while needed travels as `degraded` on REST and as a thrown error on MCP; `_provenance: 'org'` on a host row changes nothing (pinned); one holder answers exactly as before on all four doors (CONTROL pins); app-todo's ownerless host handlers are one owner per key and are not refused.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-j3zq64`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmPF1skfu2kx89BEXZi`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
